newsitem.title: GERMANY: German June BME/Reuters PMI falls but prices up.
newsitem.headline: German June BME/Reuters PMI falls but prices up.

text.p: The BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers' Index fell to a seasonally-adjusted 56.83 in June from 57.77 in May, research group NTC Publications Ltd said in a statement released on Tuesday.
On an unadjusted basis it fell to 56.62 from 57.42.
The index, available exclusively on Reuters systems, showed the second-strongest monthly improvement recorded since the survey started in April 1996, NTC said in a statement.
The fall in the index does not signal a decline in the manufacturing sector but indicates a slight slowdown in growth from May.
"Once again, it was a further strengthening of order books that encouraged manufacturers to increase output," NTC said.
The May seasonally-adjusted index was revised from an originally reported 57.49 while the May unadjusted index was unrevised.
NTC said the rising incidence of supply bottlenecks in many cases resulted in suppliers pushing up prices.
"These demand-driven price pressures, combined with the increased cost of imported materials arising from the weakness of the Deutschmark, pushed average input prices higher," NTC said.
Prices rose for the fifth month running, with an acceleration in the rate of increase.

The index is based on a survey of 350 companies carried out exclusively for Reuters by research group NTC Publications Ltd in cooperation with the BME German Association for Materials Management, Purchasing and Logistics.
NOTE - The PMI is modelled on the closely watched U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index.

A reading below 50 percent indicates that the manufacturing economy is generally declining, while a level above 50 percent shows it generally expanding. The more it deviates from 50, the greater the improvement or decline in the current month.
